notes: Rounds: Geary p833 reads 277,000 rounds expended "in the fight on July 3, and in subsequent skirmishing" - not 227,000 (W-CH) or ~250,000 (soldier's letter). The OCR digit pattern could be a misread; the library holds a single OCR witness (archive.org cu31924077699761), so a second-witness check failed to run (no second scan in the repo, none fetched this session). The OR period "July 3 and subsequent skirmishing" also differs from the row's "fight" and the seed note (Jul 2 evening-Jul 3 or Jul 3 alone). Brigade list (Daniel, Smith, O'Neal) and failed assaults supported (Johnson p504; Walker p519: five hours' incessant fire). Hours 06:00-11:00: Williams p513 says four hours from early light to ~noon; Ireland p867 first relief 5.45 a.m. Carry the numbers as a range with the OCR flag.

source_citations.author: Maj. Charles S. Peyton
source_citations.passage: Garnett's brigade reached the field about 9 a.m. (July 3)

source_citations.author: Gen. Robert E. Lee
source_citations.passage: Pickett with three brigades joined Longstreet the following morning (July 3) (audit T3-045; not re-read; Jan 1864 report differs, see audit claim g1)

notes: No OR passage says an order did or did not reach Pickett to be on the field by daylight; "preparation takes all morning" is W-PC (secondary). Related OR facts: Lee's Jul 1863 report p308 has Pickett joining Longstreet the morning of Jul 3; Peyton (Garnett's brigade) p385 says the brigade reached the field about 9 a.m.; Lee's Jan 1864 report differs (afternoon of Jul 2; audit claim g1 AMBIGUOUS). Existing registers: EG-0004, EG-0037, EG-0041, EG-0070.
